problem: Whether the variance V alone forces a universal lower bound of order 1/V on the normalized Turán deficit delta_k near the mode of a Poisson–binomial law, and the paper proves V*delta_D >= 1/4 at the first-descent index D when V >= 1.
debate: The literature on log-concavity, Turán-type and ultra-log-concavity bounds for Bernoulli sums and on mode and maximal-mass bounds (Hillion–Johnson, Johnson, Dümbgen–Wellner, Darroch, Pitman, Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne), though no named controversy is identified.
gap: Existing lower bounds on delta_k depend on n, on the success probabilities, or on k alone, and so degenerate at fixed variance when many probabilities sit near 0 or 1, whereas none is scaled by variance.
contribution: A computer-assisted proof (Bernstein expansions in exact arithmetic) that V*delta_D >= 1/4, a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3, and corollaries delta_k >= 1/(4V+|k-D|) and 1/(4V+1) <= delta_c < 2/V, with a Haar-unitary eigenvalue application giving order 1/log N against 1/N from ultra-log-concavity.
note: The result and its gap are stated plainly, but you never say why anyone needs a variance-scaled deficit lower bound beyond a normal-curvature analogy and one buried unitary-matrix example, and the constant is left open between 1/4 and 1/3, so lead with the motivation and say what the open gap costs.
